confirmed.title: Reinstating a provider unconditionally sets provider status to 'approved', bypassing the approval/background-check gate
confirmed.detail:
`setUserSuspended` flips provider status with `status: suspended ? "suspended" : "approved"`. The provider_status enum has four values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'suspended'. The action treats suspension as a simple approved⇄suspended toggle, but the target provider may currently be 'pending' or 'rejected'. Two concrete defects introduced by this diff:
1. Suspending a 'pending' or 'rejected' provider overwrites their real status with 'suspended', destroying the original state (no record of what it was).
2. Reinstating then sets status to 'approved' regardless of the pre-suspension state — silently auto-approving a provider who was never approved (e.g. one who hasn't cleared the background check, or was explicitly 'rejected'). This bypasses the M3 approval gate and is safety-relevant for a marketplace whose providers are vetted.
This is fully reachable from the UI: components/admin/UsersTable.tsx renders a Suspend button for every non-admin row (including pending/rejected providers), and components/admin/ReportCard.tsx's 'Suspend target' calls the same action.
confirmed.suggestion: Don't infer the reinstated status. Read the provider's status before suspending and, on suspend, only move 'approved' providers to 'suspended' (leave 'pending'/'rejected' as-is, or store the prior status). On reinstate, restore the saved prior status (or only un-suspend providers whose current status is 'suspended', mapping back to 'approved' only when they were approved before). Alternatively, gate the provider-status write on `target` provider status === 'approved'/'suspended' so pending/rejected providers are never auto-approved.

confirmed.title: setUserSuspended has no server-side guard against suspending an admin / itself (UI-only protection)
confirmed.detail: The UsersTable deliberately hides the suspend button for admin rows (`r.role === "admin" ? "—" : <SuspendUserButton>`), signalling intent that admins must not be suspendable. But setUserSuspended only validates `{ userId: uuid, suspended: bool }` and writes `is_suspended` for ANY target regardless of role — it even loads `target.role` but only uses it to decide whether to also flip `providers.status`, never to block admin targets. Server Actions are directly invokable POST endpoints, so any authenticated admin (the only caller that passes `requireRole("admin")`) can suspend another admin or themselves by supplying an arbitrary userId — also reachable via ReportCard's 'suspend target' button when `report.target_id` points at an admin. Impact is bounded (requires existing admin privilege; `is_suspended` on an admin currently has no login/dashboard lock-out effect since suspension is only enforced for customers), so this is not privilege escalation — but it is an unintended, server-unenforced state that the UI itself treats as forbidden.
confirmed.suggestion: In setUserSuspended, after loading `target.role`, return `{ ok: false }` (or a typed error) when `target.role === 'admin'`, mirroring the UI's exclusion. This closes the IDOR-style gap regardless of which UI path calls it.

confirmed.title: Suspension enforcement at session start is incomplete: only the customer-initiated path is blocked, and suspended providers are not blocked at all
confirmed.detail: The new guard is `if (profile?.id === booking.customer_id && profile.is_suspended) return error`. Two gaps in the brand-new suspension feature: (1) `loadBookingForParty` admits BOTH parties, so when the check subject is the provider (`profile.id === booking.provider_id`) the suspension check is skipped entirely — a provider can start the session for a suspended customer, who can then join the now-existing `in_progress` session, defeating the stated goal ('a suspended customer cannot start a call — protects providers'). (2) A SUSPENDED PROVIDER is never checked here: setUserSuspended flips `providers.status` to 'suspended' (which only removes them from browse / blocks NEW bookings via getApprovedProvider), but their existing `confirmed` bookings remain runnable, and startSession/endSession have no provider-suspension check — so a suspended provider can still run their pre-existing sessions. New-booking enforcement is sound (customer's is_suspended checked in createBooking; suspended providers excluded by getApprovedProvider), but the at-call enforcement does not fully cover either suspended party.
confirmed.suggestion: In startSession, after loading the booking, fetch both parties' suspension state and block the call if EITHER `booking.customer_id` or `booking.provider_id` is suspended (e.g. check `profiles.is_suspended` for both ids, or check `providers.status = 'suspended'` for the provider), independent of which party invoked the action.

confirmed.title: Activity-table status badges expose raw enum tokens with no icon (machine text, color-only reinforcement)
confirmed.detail: The Sessions/Payments/Payouts tables render status via <Badge tone={...} label={r.status} /> where r.status is the raw database enum string — so screen-reader and sighted users see unlabeled machine tokens like "in_progress", "captured", "authorized", "scheduled" instead of human copy. This also violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing copy through messages/en.json) — note the table headers ARE translated (t("admin.colStatus")) but the cell values are not. Additionally, the local Badge wrapper (line 50-51) calls <StatusBadge tone> WITHOUT an icon, unlike every other status pill in the app (provider/PayoutsTable, IncomingRequests, customer/UpcomingBookings, and even the sibling UsersTable all pass an `icon`). StatusBadge's own contract says meaning should be carried by icon + text together, with tone as reinforcement; here a colored pill plus a raw token is the only signal, weakening the no-color-alone guarantee for distinguishing e.g. failed vs captured payments.
confirmed.suggestion: Map each status enum to a translated label (en.json keys) and a paired Lucide icon before rendering, mirroring PayoutsTable (t("provider.payoutPaid") + CalendarCheck). E.g. a STATUS_META record per table giving { label: t(...), icon } and pass both to StatusBadge so the cell shows readable copy and an icon, not the raw token.

confirmed.location: SESSION_TONE / PAYMENT_TONE / PAYOUT_TONE maps + the status column render() calls (label={r.status})
confirmed.title: Admin activity tables render raw DB status strings as user-facing labels (bypasses i18n, inconsistent with every other table)
confirmed.detail: The three status columns render the raw database enum value directly: `render: (r) => <Badge tone={SESSION_TONE[r.status] ?? "neutral"} label={r.status} />`. So users see developer-facing strings like "in_progress", "captured", "authorized", "refunded", "scheduled" verbatim. This violates CLAUDE.md golden rule #7 (all user-facing copy goes through messages/en.json) and is inconsistent with the rest of the app: the customer account page already defines a localized status map (app/(customer)/account/page.tsx PAY_STATUS → account.payAuthorized/payCaptured/...), and components/provider/PayoutsTable.tsx / customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx render StatusBadge with localized labels via ternaries. The new code re-invents tone lookup maps but skips the label localization those patterns provide. Note also the trivial local `Badge` wrapper around StatusBadge adds nothing — other tables pass children directly to StatusBadge.
confirmed.suggestion: Make each TONE map carry both a tone and a message key (mirroring account.page PAY_STATUS), add keys like admin.statusInProgress/Captured/Authorized/Refunded/Scheduled/Completed/Paid/Failed to messages/en.json, and render t(key) instead of r.status. Drop the one-line Badge wrapper and use <StatusBadge tone={...}>{t(label)}</StatusBadge> directly for consistency.

confirmed.title: Row action buttons have identical, ambiguous accessible names across rows
confirmed.detail: In the Users table, every row renders <SuspendUserButton> whose visible label/accessible name is just t("admin.suspend") = "Suspend" (or "Reinstate"). The user's `name` prop is passed in but only used inside the toast/announce string (SuspendUserButton.tsx:33-34) — it is never surfaced on the button itself (no aria-label / aria-describedby). So a screen-reader user navigating by buttons (or the WCAG 2.4.4 / 4.1.2 "buttons with the same name must have the same/ disambiguated purpose" expectation) hears "Suspend, button" repeated for every active user with no way to tell which user each one acts on. The same applies to ReportCard's "Mark reviewed" and "Suspend the reported user" buttons, which repeat verbatim across every report card. This is confirmed by the test (tests/component/admin-dashboard.test.tsx:65) which can only query getByRole('button',{name:/^suspend$/i}) because the fixture happens to contain exactly one suspendable active non-admin user; with two it would match multiple elements. axe does not auto-flag duplicate accessible names, so the axe assertion passes while the real ambiguity remains. Note: provider/listener dashboards (e.g. provider session links) typically carry the subject name in the control's context; this admin table does not.
confirmed.suggestion: Give each row action an unambiguous accessible name that includes the subject, e.g. pass an aria-label like t("admin.suspendUser", { name }) / t("admin.reinstateUser", { name }) to the Button in SuspendUserButton, and aria-label including reporter/target on ReportCard's buttons. Add the corresponding keys to messages/en.json (keeping the visible short text via children while the aria-label carries the full context).

confirmed.title: Server action lets an admin suspend an admin / themselves; UI invariant not enforced server-side
confirmed.detail: UsersTable.tsx deliberately renders no suspend button for rows where role === 'admin' (and the test asserts this), establishing the invariant that admins are not suspendable. But the server action setUserSuspended only checks requireRole('admin') and validates the UUID — it does not check the target's role. An admin can therefore suspend another admin or themselves by invoking the action directly (e.g. via ReportCard's suspendTarget with an admin target_id, or a crafted call). Today the blast radius is limited because is_suspended is only enforced for customers in booking/session and is not checked at admin login, so a suspended admin is not actually locked out — but the data ends up in a state the UI treats as impossible, and the safety net is missing if is_suspended enforcement is later broadened.
confirmed.suggestion: After loading `target.role`, reject suspension of admins server-side: `if (target.role === 'admin') return { ok: false };` (optionally also guard against self-suspension by comparing userId to the calling admin's id). This makes the server enforce the same invariant the UI already assumes.

confirmed.title: Admin user search has no live result-count / no-results announcement
confirmed.detail:
AdminUserSearch submits by router.push to /admin/users?q=…, which re-renders the server component and the table in place. There is no aria-live region announcing how many users matched or that none did. The DataTable's emptyText is shown but it sits in a plain , not a live region, so it is not announced after an in-place navigation. This is a regression relative to the codebase's own established pattern: app/(customer)/browse/page.tsx:55-56 wraps its result count in

{t("browse.resultsCount", { count })}

. A blind admin filtering users gets no feedback that the search ran or returned nothing.
confirmed.suggestion: Add an aria-live="polite" element to the users page showing the result count (e.g. t("admin.usersResultsCount", { count: users.length })) above the table, matching the browse page pattern, with a corresponding en.json key.

confirmed.title: Hardcoded user-facing string bypasses messages/en.json
confirmed.detail: The suspended-customer guard introduced by M13 returns a hardcoded English string: `return { error: "Your account is paused. Please contact support." };`. This violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing copy goes through messages/en.json). A suitable key already exists from this same milestone — `booking.suspended` ("Your account is paused. Please contact support to continue.") is used by the parallel guard in app/(customer)/actions.ts:26 via t(). The sibling createBooking guard does it correctly; only this new session-start guard hardcodes the copy. (The other hardcoded strings in this file on lines 47 and 85 are pre-existing, not introduced by this diff.)
confirmed.suggestion: Import is already there for t-style usage in the customer actions; reuse the existing key, e.g. `return { error: t("booking.suspended") };` (add the t import to this file as done in app/(customer)/actions.ts).

confirmed.title: Suspension message hardcoded here but localized (t("booking.suspended")) in the sibling booking action added by the same milestone
confirmed.detail: This diff adds `return { error: "Your account is paused. Please contact support." }` for suspended customers. The same M13 diff added a booking.suspended key to messages/en.json and used `t("booking.suspended")` in app/(customer)/actions.ts createBooking for the exact same concept. The discrepancy is mild because session/actions.ts already had pre-existing hardcoded English error strings (it does not import t), so the new line is locally consistent — but it diverges from the i18n approach the milestone itself chose for the parallel suspension message.
confirmed.suggestion: For consistency within the milestone, import t and reuse a shared suspension key (e.g. t("booking.suspended") or a new session.suspended key) instead of a fresh hardcoded English string. If the team intends to leave session/actions.ts non-i18n for now, leave as-is — but then the createBooking suspension copy should arguably match that choice.

confirmed.title: User-supplied admin search term is interpolated unescaped into a PostgREST .or() filter (filter-injection pattern)
confirmed.detail: `listUsers` builds `query.or(`full_name.ilike.${term},email.ilike.${term}`)` where `term = `%${search.trim()}%`` comes straight from the `?q=` query param (AdminUserSearch form). PostgREST parses the .or() string as filter syntax, so characters such as `,`, `(`, `)`, `.` in the search term can break out of the intended two ilike conditions and inject additional OR clauses or trigger a 400. This is the only `.or()` interpolation in the codebase and is introduced by this diff. Security impact is low because the caller is always an admin (route guard + RLS `is_admin()` on profiles), so no data the admin couldn't already read is exposed — but it is a new unsanitized-input-into-query-DSL pattern that can cause unexpected filtering or errors.
confirmed.suggestion: Escape/sanitize the term before interpolation — at minimum strip or reject PostgREST reserved characters (`,()`. backslash, `*`), or wrap the value in double quotes per PostgREST quoting rules, or use Supabase `.ilike()` calls combined via `.or()` with properly quoted values.

confirmed.title: Admin user search interpolates raw input into a PostgREST .or() filter string (latent injection / breaks on special chars)
confirmed.detail: `listUsers` builds `term = "%" + search.trim() + "%"` and interpolates it directly into `query.or(`full_name.ilike.${term},email.ilike.${term}`)`. PostgREST parses the .or() argument as a filter grammar where ',' separates conditions and '(' ')' group them. Unescaped user input therefore (a) breaks legitimate searches — searching a name containing a comma or parentheses (e.g. "Smith, John" or "(work)") splits/garbles the filter or 400s, and (b) is a latent filter-injection pattern (an attacker-controlled value can append extra OR conditions like `,role.eq.admin`). The security blast radius is limited because the call is behind requireRole("admin") and targets profiles, which admins can already read in full via RLS — so there is no privilege escalation or data exposure beyond what the admin already has. Severity is low for that reason, but the correctness bug on normal inputs is real and this is the only .or() string in the codebase.
confirmed.suggestion: Avoid embedding raw input in the .or() filter string. Either escape PostgREST-reserved characters (wrap the value in double quotes for like/ilike and strip/escape internal quotes), or replace the single .or() with a safer construction (e.g. two separate ilike queries unioned in JS, or quote the pattern: `full_name.ilike."${escaped}"`). At minimum sanitize commas/parentheses/asterisks before interpolation.

confirmed.title: Dead message key: nav.providers is now orphaned
confirmed.detail: components/shared/AppHeader.tsx previously had the admin nav point at { href: "/admin/providers", labelKey: "nav.providers" }, and that was the only consumer of nav.providers. This diff replaces it with labelKey "admin.navApprovals" and removes nav.providers from the labelKey union type. Grep confirms no remaining reference to nav.providers anywhere in the codebase, so the key is now dead.
confirmed.suggestion: Remove the orphaned "providers": "Listeners" entry from the nav block in messages/en.json (or repurpose it if intentionally kept for future use).
